# Translating the Tools {#sec-translating-tools}

This book teaches each capture point with an R tool. The
ideas do not depend on R. A lockfile, a container, a
literate document, a pipeline, a test, and a continuous
integration run each have counterparts in other
languages. A reader who works in Python or Stata can
apply the chapters by substituting them.
@tbl-translating-tools gives the substitutions we could
confirm against each tool's own documentation, opened on
26 November 2026. An empty cell means we did not confirm
an equivalent, not that none exists. Nothing in the core
chapters depends on this appendix.

| Capture point | This book (R) | Python | Stata |
|---|---|---|---|
| Version control (@sec-version-control) | `git` | `git` | `git`, for do-files and ado-files |
| Package versions (@sec-dependencies) | `renv` and `renv.lock` | `uv` and `uv.lock`; or `pixi` and `pixi.lock` | |
| Language behavior across releases | The R version recorded in `renv.lock` and fixed by the image | | A `version` statement at the top of every do-file |
| Environment (@sec-containers) | A Docker image built from a digest-pinned base | The same Docker recipe, with Python in place of R | |
| Literate document (@sec-literate) | Quarto with the `knitr` engine | A Jupyter notebook, or a `.qmd` file, rendered by Quarto | `dyndoc`, to HTML or Word |
| Pipeline (@sec-pipelines) | `targets` | Snakemake | |
| Tests and checks (@sec-testing) | `tinytest`, and `stopifnot()` for data | `pytest` | `assert`, for data |
| Continuous integration (@sec-verification) | GitHub Actions with `r-lib/actions` | GitHub Actions with `actions/setup-python` and `pytest` | |

: This book's R tools and their counterparts in Python and Stata {#tbl-translating-tools}

Each Python and Stata entry rests on the source below.

- **`uv.lock`.** The `uv` documentation describes it as
  recording the exact resolved versions installed in the
  project environment, across operating systems,
  architectures, and Python versions. It says the file
  'should be checked into version control'
  (<https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/layout/>).
- **`pixi.lock`.** The `pixi` documentation describes a
  lock file listing the exact dependencies resolved for
  every environment and platform in the manifest, and
  argues for committing it, with an exception for library
  projects (<https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/workspace/lock_file/>).
  @sec-backends discusses `pixi` with the rest of the
  conda family.
- **Stata `version`.** The Stata manual advises typing
  `version` at the top of every do-file, so that the
  do-file 'will continue to run in all future versions of
  Stata'. The version setting also selects the
  random-number generator
  (<https://www.stata.com/manuals/pversion.pdf>). It fixes
  how the interpreter behaves, not which add-on packages
  are installed, so it is not a lockfile.
- **Jupyter and Quarto.** In Jupyter's own words, a
  notebook is 'a shareable document that combines computer
  code, plain language descriptions, data, rich
  visualizations like 3D models, charts, graphs and
  figures, and interactive controls'
  (<https://docs.jupyter.org/en/latest/>). Quarto renders
  a notebook, but does not execute its cells unless asked
  to with `--execute`
  (<https://quarto.org/docs/computations/python.html>).
  The hidden-state landmine of @sec-literate applies with
  particular force to notebooks.
- **`dyndoc`.** Stata's `dyndoc` converts a Markdown
  document containing Stata commands to HTML or a Word
  document, running the commands and inserting their
  output (<https://www.stata.com/manuals/rptdyndoc.pdf>).
- **Snakemake.** 'A tool to create reproducible and
  scalable data analyses', in its documentation's words
  (<https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/>). In a
  Python project it plays the role that @sec-pipelines
  gives to `targets`.
- **`pytest`.** A framework that 'makes it easy to write
  small, readable tests' (<https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/>).
- **Stata `assert`.** It verifies that an expression is
  true and, if not, stops with return code 9
  (<https://www.stata.com/manuals/dassert.pdf>), which makes
  it the counterpart of `stopifnot()` after a merge or a
  recode.
- **Python on GitHub Actions.** GitHub's guide 'Building
  and testing Python' sets up Python with
  `actions/setup-python` and runs `pytest`
  (<https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/build-and-test-code/python>).

Two cautions apply to every row. First, a counterpart
reaches the same rung only if it is used the same way:
a `uv.lock` that is not committed pins nothing, and a
notebook rendered from stored outputs is not a fresh
render. Second, Stata is licensed software, and we did not
check how its license applies inside a container or to a
deposited image, so the table leaves the Stata
environment cell empty.
